draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Topslip! The name comes from a 19th century local practice of sliding timber logs down the hills from right here, and today it's the main visitor base of the Anamalai Tiger Reserve, with the tea town of Valparai up in the same hills.
draft.hungryLine: Up here it's all about a hot cup of tea from any small tea stall, and in Valparai town the messes do proper breakfast, lunch and dinner.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Explore the Anamalai Tiger Reserve from Topslip, then head up to Valparai and drive 15 km out to Chinnakallar's misty forest and roaring falls.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit with a hot tea at a small stall in Valparai, surrounded by the town's 56 tea and coffee estates.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Chinnakallar, 15 km from Valparai, is the second highest rainfall area in India, and its waterfall is said to sound like a roaring lion.

spots.name: Anamalai Tiger Reserve
spots.detail: Right here · Tiger reserve in the Anaimalai Hills, with its tourist facilities at Topslip

spots.name: Chinnakallar
spots.detail: 15 km from Valparai · Wet, misty forest road and a thundering waterfall

spots.name: Grass Hills
spots.detail: Valparai hills · Grassland at around 2400 m, home of the Nilgiri Thar

legends.title: Sliding the logs
legends.body: Back in the 1800s, timber was sent sliding down the hills from this spot. That old habit is how Topslip got its name.

tips.title: Get permission for Grass Hills.
tips.body: It's a restricted area, so you need prior permission from the Chief Wildlife Warden, Chennai, before you go.

tips.title: Leave the alcohol behind.
tips.body: Forest officials strictly prohibit alcohol here, so stick to tea and water.

story.title: First coffee
story.body: The earliest records of Valparai start in 1846, when K. Ramasamy Mudaliyar started a coffee plantation. By the mid-1800s, much of the plateau was under tea or coffee.

story.title: Timber slides
story.body: Loggers slid timber down the hills from Topslip, giving the place its name. In 1864 the Karnatic Coffee Company tried its luck here too, but sold off part of its land.

story.title: A prime minister visits
story.body: Indira Gandhi visited the park on 7 October 1961. It was later named Indira Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary and National Park after her.

story.title: Tiger reserve
story.body: On 27 June 2007, the sanctuary was declared the Anaimalai Tiger Reserve. Its core and buffer areas now cover 1479.87 km2.
